seat_fill_rate.basis: DGT/DITE tracer rates; replace when district MIS actual fill is available

completion_rate.basis: DGT/DITE tracer rates; replace when district MIS actual completion is available

sector_entry_rate.basis: explicit analyst prior pending district placement data

decision_rule: GAP if p90<1; SURPLUS if p10>1; otherwise NEEDS DATA
sci_formula: weighted share of openings covered at R=min(S/D,1)
assumption_note: State manufacturing employment comes from ASI. District demand is allocated using one of three transparent Udyam bases: employment share, enterprise-unit share, or their 50/50 blend. Allocator choice is structural uncertainty; rank stability is reported across all three. NCO mix is an analyst prior until PLFS unit-level occupation-by-industry data is loaded. District ITI supply remains provisional/partial in the public DGT evidence.
occupation_share_note: Selected NCO shares are fractions of total manufacturing employment. 0.25 + 0.15 = 0.40 is modeled; 0.60 remains outside the two-group pilot scope.
supply_note: Pilot is restricted to NCO groups 72 and 74. Group 81 is intentionally excluded because the current ITI crosswalk support is weak for a defensible trade-to-occupation demonstration.
proxy_supply_note: District proxy supply is allocated from 2022 official district ITI counts (CTS) as within-division weights, scaled to the current NCVT state seat magnitude. These are historical weights, not current district seat totals. Full current NCVT district trade data should replace them for policy calls.
actual_supply_note: The bundled NCVT file is an indexed partial sample, not a downloaded complete extract. Full district-wide policy eligibility requires a supplied file marked coverage_status=full_district_extract and covering all 31 districts and modeled NCO groups.
headline_note: Proxy-only SCI is a relative prioritisation index; it is not a district skill-gap finding. Partial NCVT evidence is treated as a floor plus uncertain remainder. Only full district coverage can unlock a provisional policy call.

demand_allocation_uncertainty.basis: Within-allocator district allocation uncertainty prior; sigma 0.35 has no empirical district calibration. Structural allocator uncertainty is assessed separately across employment, enterprise-unit and blended shares.

analytical_geography_note: Raw LGD has 31 districts; proxy analysis uses 30 analytical geographies by merging Ballari and Vijayanagara because the 2022 CTS source reports historical Bellary as one geography.
iti_weight_verification_note: 30/30 analytical ITI weights reproduce the bundled machine-extracted Annexure-IV transcription (Govt, Private, Total). This check does not independently prove the source PDF binary; visual verification against the government PDF is still required. Weights are historical 2022 allocation weights only.
out_of_scope_note: DGT trades outside NCO 72/74 are explicitly labelled OUT_OF_SCOPE in the pilot crosswalk. Their seats remain in the published seat total and are reported separately from truly UNMAPPED seats.

dgt_share_allocation_uncertainty.basis: Dirichlet concentration 18 with 75% retention of the blended evidence-weighted mean; analyst choice to widen uncertainty without collapsing small districts to zero.

dgt_share_note: DGT 2026 district/group seats are blended toward the historical 2022 ITI-count proxy using district matrix coverage = DGT ITIs in matrix / 2022 ITI count. This prevents sparse matrix coverage from creating artificial zero-supply districts. The blended distribution is still provisional and remains NEEDS DATA.
demand_allocation_source_note: Demand allocator sensitivity compares Udyam employment shares, Udyam enterprise-unit shares (June 2026), and their 50/50 blend. The blend is an arbitrary midpoint sensitivity case, not an empirically calibrated estimator; the two bases measure different underlying concepts. Allocator choice is structural uncertainty; district priority is robust only when the rank persists across the alternatives.
